blurb: Mascots, taglines and the surprising stories behind big brands

questions.q: Which cereal mascot, introduced in 1952, says Frosted Flakes are 'Gr-r-reat!'?
questions.fact: Tony was created at the Leo Burnett ad agency, where art director Eugene Kolkey designed the original tiger.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_the_Tiger (debuted 1952 for Frosted Flakes; Kolkey, Leo Burnett art director, designed Tony; catchphrase came from voice actor Thurl Ravenscroft, from 1953)

questions.q: The pink Energizer Bunny began in 1988 as a spoof of a bunny ad from which rival battery brand?
questions.fact: Duracell's drumming bunny dates to 1973, but a 1992 settlement gave Energizer the bunny rights in the US and Canada.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energizer_Bunny (first ad 1988, parody of Duracell Bunny; Duracell bunny 1973; Jan 10, 1992 settlement: Energizer exclusive US/Canada rights)

questions.q: The GEICO Gecko made his first appearance in a TV ad in which year?
questions.fact: The Martin Agency of Richmond, Virginia created him for a single spot; he wasn't meant to become a campaign.
questions.src: shootonline.com/?p=11988 (July 1999 spot 'Press Conference'; Martin Agency's Steve Bassett: 'It wasn't meant to be a campaign')

questions.q: The Michelin Man, created in the 1890s, has what official name?
questions.fact: Tires were a pale gray-white when he was created; they turned black around 1912, when carbon was added to the rubber.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelin_Man (official name Bibendum; introduced 1894 Lyon exhibition; tires originally gray-white, black from 1912 when carbon added)

questions.q: Which brand adopted the slogan 'Just Do It' in 1988?
questions.fact: Dan Wieden of Wieden+Kennedy, an ad agency based in Portland, Oregon, wrote the line.
questions.src: fox6now.com/sports/dan-wieden-ad-icon-behind-nikes-just-do-it-slogan-dies (Wieden 'famously coined the Nike tagline Just Do It. in 1988', Portland dateline); dezeen.com 2015/03/14 article on Wieden+Kennedy

questions.q: The 'Got Milk?' ad campaign began in 1993 for milk processors in which state?
questions.fact: Ad agency Goodby Silverstein & Partners created it for the California Milk Processor Board.
questions.src: Wikipedia, Got Milk? (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Got_Milk%3F): created by Goodby Silverstein & Partners for the California Milk Processor Board in 1993

questions.q: 'Can you hear me now?' was the 2000s ad catchphrase of which wireless carrier?
questions.fact: Actor Paul Marcarelli played the 'Test Man' from 2002 to 2011, then turned up in Sprint ads in 2016.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Marcarelli (Verizon Test Man 2002 to April 2011; Sprint spokesman 2016)

questions.q: Which car rental company made being No. 2 a selling point with its 1962 slogan 'We Try Harder'?
questions.fact: The campaign came from ad agency Doyle Dane Bernbach and openly admitted that Avis trailed Hertz.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Bernbach (debuted 1962 as Avis lost share to Hertz); wiki/Avis_Rent_a_Car_System (motto adopted 1962, spin on No. 2 status vs larger Hertz); wiki/Doyle_Dane_Bernbach ('We Try Harder Because We're Number 2')

questions.q: Twitter's bird logo was nicknamed Larry, after which Boston Celtics legend?
questions.fact: Twitter co-founder Biz Stone confirmed the bird's namesake in a 2011 tweet.
questions.src: wrtv.com/sports/pacers/did-you-know-the-twitter-logo-was-named-after-larry-bird (Biz Stone tweet, Aug 11, 2011)

questions.q: IKEA's name starts with its founder's initials. In which country did he start it in 1943?
questions.fact: Ingvar Kamprad was 17; the E and A stand for Elmtaryd, his family farm, and Agunnaryd, his home village.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IKEA (founded 1943 in Sweden by 17-year-old Ingvar Kamprad; Elmtaryd farm, Agunnaryd village)

questions.q: Long before phones, Nokia began in 1865 as a Finnish mill serving which industry?
questions.fact: Fredrik Idestam's first mill made wood pulp; the name comes from the town of Nokia and its Nokianvirta River.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Nokia (1865 ground wood pulp mill, Tammerkoski rapids, Tampere, Fredrik Idestam; name derived from town of Nokia and Nokianvirta River)

questions.q: Audi's four rings stand for four carmakers that merged in 1932. What was the new company called?
questions.fact: The four were Audi, DKW, Horch and Wanderer; the interlocking rings symbolize their unity.
questions.src: audi.com/en/company/history/four-brands-four-rings.html (Auto Union formed 29 June 1932; Audi, DKW, Horch, Wanderer; rings symbolise unity of the four)

blurb: Department stores, discount giants and how we learned to shop

questions.q: What is the name of Target's white bull terrier mascot?
questions.fact: Target was launched by the Dayton Company, owner of the Dayton's department stores in Minneapolis.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Target_Corporation (Bullseye, white Bull Terrier; Target launched by John Geisse and Douglas Dayton for the Dayton Company)

questions.q: The first Walmart, Kmart and Target stores all opened in the same year. Which year?
questions.fact: The first Target opened in Roseville, Minnesota, in May, and the first Walmart in Rogers, Arkansas, on July 2.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walmart (Rogers, AR, July 2, 1962); wiki/Target_Corporation (Roseville, MN, May 1962); wiki/Kmart (first Kmart-named store San Fernando, CA, Jan 25, 1962; first full-size Garden City, MI, Mar 1, 1962)

questions.q: James Cash Penney opened his first store, a Golden Rule shop, in 1902 in which state?
questions.fact: He opened it on April 14, 1902, in the small town of Kemmerer, in partnership with two other merchants.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JCPenney (Kemmerer, Wyoming, April 14, 1902; partners Thomas Callahan and Guy Johnson)

questions.q: Before his famous catalog, Richard Sears got started in 1886 selling what by mail?
questions.fact: Sears later sold entire kit houses by mail order, from 1908 to 1940.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sears (R.W. Sears Watch Company, Minneapolis, 1886; Sears Catalog Home kits 1908-1940)

questions.q: Which shopping invention did Sylvan Goldman introduce in 1937 at his Oklahoma City stores?
questions.fact: Shoppers balked at first, so Goldman hired models to push the carts around his Humpty Dumpty stores.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvan_Goldman (June 4, 1937, Humpty Dumpty chain, Oklahoma City; hired male and female models to push carts)

questions.q: In 1974, the first product scanned by a UPC barcode at a supermarket was a pack of what?
questions.fact: It was a 10-pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit, scanned at 8:01 a.m. at a Marsh supermarket in Troy, Ohio.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Product_Code (10-pack Wrigley's Juicy Fruit, Marsh supermarket, Troy OH, 8:01 a.m. June 26, 1974; only a facsimile went to the Smithsonian, so that claim was dropped)

questions.q: The first fully enclosed, climate-controlled US shopping mall opened in 1956 in which state?
questions.fact: Southdale Center in Edina was designed by Austrian-born architect Victor Gruen.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southdale_Center (opened Oct 8, 1956, Edina MN; 'first fully enclosed, climate-controlled shopping mall in the United States'; Victor Gruen, native of Vienna)

questions.q: Piggly Wiggly, called the first true self-service grocery store, opened in 1916 in which city?
questions.fact: Founder Clarence Saunders even received a patent for his 'self-serving store' in 1917.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piggly_Wiggly (Memphis, 1916; 'first true self-service grocery store'; US Patent 1,242,872 'Self-serving store', Oct 9, 1917)

questions.q: Black Friday falls on the day after which US holiday?
questions.fact: The name caught on in Philadelphia, where police used it by 1961 to describe the day's crowds and traffic jams.
questions.src: history.com/news/black-friday-thanksgiving-origins-history (Philadelphia police, 1950s; caption dates the name to 1961)

questions.q: In 1917, which company's Kansas City store ran out of tissue paper and ended up launching modern gift wrap?
questions.fact: Out of red, green and white tissue at Christmas, the Hall brothers sold imported French paper instead, at a dime a sheet.
questions.src: corporate.hallmark.com/Product/Gift-Wrap-Overview (Christmas 1917, Hall Brothers' Kansas City store ran out of tissue; imported French decorative paper at a dime a sheet; credited with founding modern gift wrap industry). Replaces Rudolph/Montgomery Ward, which duplicates holiday-hits (A1) Origin Stories 400.

questions.q: Which credit card company launched Small Business Saturday in 2010?
questions.fact: It falls on the Saturday after Thanksgiving, sandwiched between Black Friday and Cyber Monday.
questions.src: americanexpress.com/us/small-business/shop-small/supporters ('founded by American Express in 2010'; Saturday after Thanksgiving)

questions.q: GivingTuesday, the Tuesday after Thanksgiving, was started in 2012 at which New York institution?
questions.fact: Henry Timms launched it there, with the United Nations Foundation as a co-founding partner.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GivingTuesday (initiated 2012 by Henry Timms at the 92nd Street Y; co-founding organization the United Nations Foundation)

blurb: From garage startups to Cyber Monday: computers and the web

questions.q: Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded which company in 1975?
questions.fact: It began in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and moved to Bellevue, Washington, in January 1979.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft (established Apr 4, 1975, Albuquerque; HQ to Bellevue Jan 1979)

questions.q: Yahoo began in 1994 as a website guide made by two graduate students at which university?
questions.fact: Jerry Yang and David Filo first called it 'Jerry and David's Guide to the World Wide Web.'
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahoo (founded Jan 1994 by Jerry Yang and David Filo, electrical engineering graduate students at Stanford; began as 'Jerry and David's guide to the World Wide Web', renamed Yahoo! March 1994). Replaces Google/googol, which duplicates by-the-numbers (A5) Math Magic 300.

questions.q: Apple's three co-founders in 1976 were Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and who?
questions.fact: Wayne sold his share back to Jobs and Wozniak for $800, just 12 days after Apple's April 1, 1976 founding.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. (founded April 1, 1976 by Jobs, Wozniak, Wayne; Wayne sold share back for $800 twelve days later)

questions.q: In 1939, Bill Hewlett and Dave Packard formed HP in a garage in which California city?
questions.fact: The garage, at 367 Addison Avenue, is a California Historical Landmark called the Birthplace of Silicon Valley.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HP_Garage (367 Addison Ave, Palo Alto; used from 1938, partnership formed 1939; California Historical Landmark No. 976, 'Birthplace of Silicon Valley')

questions.q: Amazon got its start in 1995 by selling what online?
questions.fact: Jeff Bezos first called the company Cadabra before settling on the name Amazon.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Amazon (incorporated as Cadabra, Inc., July 1994, renamed Amazon.com; opened as online bookseller July 16, 1995)

questions.q: Who invented the World Wide Web while working at CERN in 1989?
questions.fact: The first website, at info.cern.ch, was all about the World Wide Web project itself.
questions.src: home.cern/science/computing/the-birth-of-the-web/short-history-web/ (Berners-Lee first proposal March 1989 at CERN; info.cern.ch first website, its pages about the WWW project). Old fact's 'went online in 1991' dropped: CERN had the server running by end of 1990.

questions.q: The online-shopping term 'Cyber Monday' was coined in which year?
questions.fact: Ellen Davis of the National Retail Federation introduced it in a November 28, 2005 press release.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyber_Monday ('Ellen Davis of the National Retail Federation coined the term ... in a press release on November 28, 2005')

questions.q: In 1995, eBay, then called AuctionWeb, famously sold which broken item for $14.83?
questions.fact: Founder Pierre Omidyar checked whether the buyer knew it was broken. The reply: he collected broken laser pointers.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EBay (founded as AuctionWeb Sept 3, 1995; broken laser pointer $14.83; buyer: 'I'm a collector of broken laser pointers'). Wikipedia says 'one of the first items sold', so the 'first thing sold' claim was dropped.

questions.q: How many bits make up one byte?
questions.fact: Eight bits can form 256 different patterns, enough to code every letter, digit and symbol on a keyboard.
questions.src: Textbook (8 bits = 2^8 = 256 values)

questions.q: In 1947, engineers found what creature stuck in a Harvard computer, logging an actual 'bug'?
questions.fact: The moth was taped into the team's logbook, which is now at the Smithsonian's American history museum.
questions.src: daily.jstor.org/the-bug-in-the-computer-bug-story/ (Harvard Mark II, 1947, moth taped into logbook 'first actual case of bug being found'; logbook with moth at Smithsonian National Museum of American History)

questions.q: Junk email is called 'spam' thanks to a 1970 comedy sketch by which group?
questions.fact: In the sketch, a cafe serves Spam in almost every dish while a group of Vikings sings about it.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spam_(Monty_Python_sketch) (premiered 15 Dec 1970; Green Midget Cafe; Vikings singing about Spam; term for unsolicited electronic messages derived from it)

questions.q: Bluetooth is named after Harald Bluetooth, a 10th-century king of which country?
questions.fact: Intel's Jim Kardach proposed the name in 1997: Harald united Danish tribes, much as Bluetooth unites devices.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluetooth (10th-century Danish king Harald Bluetooth, united Danish tribes; name proposed by Intel's Jim Kardach in 1997). Norway deliberately not an option since Harald also ruled it.

blurb: Coins, cash and the curious history of how we pay

questions.q: Which president first appeared on the US one-cent coin in 1909?
questions.fact: 1909 marked 100 years since Lincoln's birth, and his cent was the first regular US coin to show a real person.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_cent ('before the Lincoln cent, no regularly circulating U.S. coin had featured an actual person'; 1909 centennial of birth); usmint.gov history-of-presidents-on-our-coins (first president on a circulating coin, 1909)

questions.q: In old American slang, how much money is 'two bits'?
questions.fact: A 'bit' was one-eighth of a Spanish silver dollar, a coin widely used in early America.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bit_(money) (1 real = 1 bit = 1/8 Spanish dollar; two bits = 25 cents; Spanish dollar most common currency in colonial America)

questions.q: A US nickel is made mostly of which metal?
questions.fact: The copper-nickel five-cent coin dates to 1866, and its alloy is 75% copper and only 25% nickel.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickel_(United_States_coin) (cupronickel 75% Cu / 25% Ni, issued since 1866; Shield nickel 1866-1883; wartime 1942-45 silver alloy also mostly copper)

questions.q: Which state's coin led off the 50 State Quarters program in 1999?
questions.fact: Quarters came out in the order states ratified the Constitution or joined the Union, and Delaware was first.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50_State_quarters (1999-2008; released in order states ratified the Constitution or were admitted; Delaware first, Jan 1999)

questions.q: Whose portrait appears on the US $100 bill?
questions.fact: The very first $100 Federal Reserve note, issued in 1914, already showed Franklin, who was never president.
questions.src: uscurrency.gov/sites/default/files/downloadable-materials/files/100_1914-1990_features.pdf (1914: 'The first $100 Federal Reserve note is issued', features portrait of Benjamin Franklin). Old wording 'first appeared on the $100 in 1914' not directly stated by source, so reworded to what it says.

questions.q: US paper money is made mostly from what material?
questions.fact: The paper is three-fourths cotton and one-fourth linen, which makes bills far sturdier than ordinary paper.
questions.src: uscurrency.gov 100_1914-1990_features.pdf ('Federal Reserve note paper is one-fourth linen and three-fourths cotton'). 'Survives the wash' claim dropped as unsourced.

questions.q: Which country is credited with issuing the world's first paper money?
questions.fact: Song dynasty China used paper notes called jiaozi as early as the 11th century.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiaozi_(currency) (Song dynasty, around the 11th century, Chengdu, Sichuan; numismatists regard it as first paper money in history)

questions.q: The word 'dollar' comes from 'thaler,' a silver coin first minted in what is now which country?
questions.fact: The name comes from Joachimsthal, a Bohemian valley town whose silver mines supplied the coins.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thaler and etymonline.com/word/dollar (Joachimsthaler, Joachimsthal, Bohemia = Jachymov, Czech Republic; mine opened 1516, coins from 1518/1519; earlier Tyrolean Guldengroschen was not called a thaler, and Austria/Germany are not options)

questions.q: What does ATM stand for?
questions.fact: One of the world's first cash machines was installed at a Barclays branch in Enfield, London, on June 27, 1967.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Bank,_Enfield (installed 27 June 1967; called the world's first cash machine). Note: Wikipedia also uses 'automatic teller machine'; no option uses that form, so no second answer.

questions.q: Which card brand was called BankAmericard when it launched in 1958?
questions.fact: It began in Fresno, California, and its card issuers adopted the name Visa in 1976.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_Inc. (BankAmericard launched Sept 18, 1958, Fresno CA; renamed Visa 1976, adopted by all licensees)

questions.q: Which 1950 card, first used at New York restaurants, is often called the first general-purpose charge card?
questions.fact: It launched with 27 participating restaurants; American Express didn't start its own charge card until 1958.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diners_Club_International (founded Feb 8, 1950; NYC restaurant concept; 27 participating restaurants at launch); wiki/Credit_card (Diners Club 'first general purpose charge card'; American Express 1958)

questions.q: When the Dow Jones Industrial Average debuted in 1896, how many stocks did it track?
questions.fact: It started at 40.94, and its name honors Charles Dow and his business partner, statistician Edward Jones.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dow_Jones_Industrial_Average (debuted May 26, 1896 with 12 industrial stocks at 40.94; named after Charles Dow and associate Edward Jones). Old fact called Dow a WSJ co-founder; source only says his newsletter was the WSJ's precursor, so reworded.
